messages:
Amanda (CS): Posting here after PineView escalated — they're seeing intermittent p99 spikes on our text-generation API only for their tenant. started ~03:10 UTC, p95 fine but p99 up to ~3s. They reported impact to user workflows.
Luis (CE): They sent samples — mostly long-context chat sessions, a few streaming calls, plus a burst of embedding requests around the same time. Noticed they have a single API key used by many internal services.
Raj (SRE): I'm looking at tenant metrics now — pinging redis/kvcache and node metrics. Can someone drop the tenant id?
Amanda (CS): tenant_id: pineview-prod-03. Customer says throughput hasn't changed on their side, but they started a marketing test around 02:50 UTC.
Raj (SRE): Thanks. Quick snapshot: overall cluster p99 increased from ~220ms to ~2.9s between 03:08-03:16 UTC. For pineview-prod-03 specifically, backend latency tail spike to 3.2s. CPU on one serving node hit 98% and NVMe I/O spiked.
Sylvia (Platform): Hmm NVMe spike + single tenant suggests noisy neighbor: long requests holding KV cache or large sequence decoding causing blocking in the runtime. Any huge context lengths in the samples?
Luis (CE): Yes multiple requests with 25k tokens-ish (they're doing transcript + summarization). One request in the sample showed chunking but full session was requested as a single prompt.
Ben (Infra): Which model variant are they hitting? Large sequence usage + CPU-bound decoding could show exactly that.
Raj (SRE): They were routed to text-gen-v2 (32k context) on shared pool. Routing logs: most of their traffic went to node srv-ptl-13 at the time. That node was also handling some other heavy tenants.
Amanda (CS): PineView asks for short-term mitigation as this is customer-facing. They can throttle client on their side but want us to fix quickly.
Raj (SRE): Immediate mitigations we can try: 1) move pineview to a dedicated slot (if available), 2) bump per-tenant concurrency limit down for shared pool to reduce head-of-line blocking, 3) enable their tenant-level priority to preempt long-lived decode tasks. I'm going to tail logs and run a repro locally.
oncall-bot: Incident marker created: #INC-2026-4132 — tenant tail latency (pineview-prod-03). Pager rota pinged.
Sylvia (Platform): For quick mitigation, I can flip a routing rule to pin pineview to an alternative pool with lower utilization (canary) for the next 10m. That avoids full migration. Would need a quick canary config change.
Raj (SRE): Do that. Also reduce `tenant_max_concurrency` on shared pool from 12 -> 4 for pineview. That will throttle the number of simultaneous decodes.
Ben (Infra): I'll check disk IO scheduling on srv-ptl-13 and temporarily isolate it from other tenant assignments. Running: ```kubectl exec -it pod/srv-ptl-13 -- sh -c "nvidia-smi && iostat -x 1 3"``` seeing heavy write/reads coincident with spikes. Looks like background batch jobs triggered on that node.
Luis (CE): I'll ask PineView to pause their marketing test or reduce their internal concurrency until we stabilize — they agreed to a 15m throttle window.
Amanda (CS): Customer confirmed throttling their client by 70% for 15m. They appreciate us moving fast.
Raj (SRE): Actions taken (03:24 UTC): 1) Sylvia applied routing rule to pin tenant to pool-canary-7, 2) reduced tenant_max_concurrency to 4 for pineview on shared pool, 3) Ben cordoned srv-ptl-13 and drained non-critical pods, 4) PineView consented to client-side throttling.
Sylvia (Platform): Routing change and concurrency update applied. Monitoring dashboards show pineview p99 dropped to ~320ms within 90s after cutover.
Raj (SRE): Confirmed. Node srv-ptl-13 still has high IO but now it doesn't serve PineView. Cluster-level p99 back to baseline ~240ms.
Luis (CE): PineView reports latency improved and user-facing errors stopped. They asked for an explanation and permanent fix.
Amanda (CS): Can we provide a short RCA and immediate recommendations to the customer? They'll want to avoid this in future.
Ben (Infra): Preliminary root cause: overlapping scheduling of background batch jobs and a tenant producing long-sequence requests led to NVMe contention and head-of-line decode blocking on shared pool node srv-ptl-13. Because pineview used a single API key across many services, bursts behaved as one high-concurrency tenant.
Sylvia (Platform): Follow-ups: 1) consider a tenant-specific allowlist to prevent placement of latency-sensitive tenants on nodes scheduled with batch workloads; 2) implement soft limits on sequence length per request with server-side advisory headers; 3) improve route balancing to spread long-context workloads across multiple nodes rather than packing.
Raj (SRE): Short-term infra fixes: add per-node IO throttling for batch jobs, add placement affinity so tenants with >8k average context length avoid nodes tagged for batch jobs, and add a fast-fail or queued ticket for requests exceeding 30s decode estimate.
Amanda (CS): I'll draft customer-facing summary: timeline, actions we took, why it happened, recommended PineView mitigations (split API key per service, client-side concurrency limits, chunking long contexts).
Luis (CE): I'll coordinate a technical call with PineView next week to discuss model/route recommendations and help them configure multi-key usage.
Raj (SRE): For internal: assign postmortem owner — Syl to lead platform changes, Raj to own node IO scheduling changes, Ben to handle placement/affinity coding, Amanda to own customer comms.
Sylvia (Platform): I'll open a follow-up ticket tracking: platform/placement-allowlist and a canary to run for the allowlist logic.
Raj (SRE): For reproducibility, steps we used: 1) identify tenant with `SELECT * FROM tenant_metrics WHERE tenant_id='pineview-prod-03' AND ts > 1769004000`, 2) `kubectl logs -n serving pod/srv-ptl-13 --since=20m | grep pineview-prod-03` to correlate request IDs, 3) run local synthetic load with long contexts: ```for i in 1..50; do curl -sS -X POST $SERVE_URL -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"input":"<25k tokens>"}'; done``` 4) observe p99 on dashboards and node-level iostat.
Ben (Infra): Note: when reproducing, throttle background batch jobs or isolate to understand IO impact. We also captured flamegraph of runtime where KV cache stalls for 300-800ms during these long decodes.
Amanda (CS): PineView wants timeline + ETA for permanent fix. Can we give rough schedule for allowlist + smarter routing?
Sylvia (Platform): Roughly: 2 weeks to implement placement allowlist and affinity changes, 1 week to roll and monitor canary, plus a follow-up improvement for advisory headers (3-4 weeks). I'll prepare a short plan.
Luis (CE): PineView asked if we can offer a temporary dedicated capacity option — I flagged this to sales.
Amanda (CS): They're okay with timeline and appreciate the short-term mitigation. I'll send note and ask them to confirm dedicated capacity interest.
Raj (SRE): Closing the immediate incident — monitoring open. Will update with postmortem link once Syl's ticket created.
oncall-bot: Incident #INC-2026-4132 status -> mitigated.
Amanda (CS): Thanks everyone. Follow-ups: postmortem, customer comms draft, and placement allowlist ticket.
Sylvia (Platform): Created internal ticket PLAT-1189 for placement allowlist and PLAT-1190 for route-balancer improvements.
Ben (Infra): I'll upload the flamegraph and iostat logs to the incident folder. link: https://redwood-internal/incident/INC-2026-4132/logs
Raj (SRE): I'll schedule a 30m retro this week to bake the fixes into runbooks.
Amanda (CS): Marking resolved for now. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Luis (CE): PineView confirmed in chat: "latency looks back to normal, huge thanks."
Amanda (CS): I'll follow up with a written RCA and the next steps for PineView.
